newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Ershad leaves for Riyadh for medicare.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Ershad leaves for Riyadh for medicare.

text.p: Bangladesh's former military ruler Hossain Mohammad Ershad left for Saudi Arabia on Monday for medical treatment, his aides said.

It is Ershad's first trip outside Bangladesh since he lost power in a 1990 people's uprising that ended his nearly nine years of rule, first as martial law administrator and then president. Ershad, 68, spent six years in prison for alleged corruption and misuse of power before being released earlier this year. He was admitted to hospital last month with heart problems.
The government recently returned his passport, allowing him to travel abroad for treatment.

"He is going to the kingdom (Saudi Arabia) for medical treatment and also to perform Umrah (pilgrimage) to Mecca at the invitation of King Fahd," retired army Major Wajed, one of Ershad's personal staff, told Reuters on Sunday.
"The King has offered him free treatment," he said. Officials at the Saudi embassy in Dhaka, however, said they had no information that the King had invited Ershad.
Wajed said Ershad might visit the United Kingdom if treatment in Saudi Arabia was not satisfactory.
Ershad is chief of the Jatiya Party, the country's third largest. He was elected a legislator of the party in June 1996 elections, which he contested from jail.
